results.evidence: Retry found only more year-dependent figures: a 2024 park conditions report describes a short mandatory lower step (~50 ft) climbed in several pitches in that season; another party reports about two full 60 m pitches of AI2; a climber's inclinometer read 35 degrees overall and 42-44 at the steepest. No two independent sources give one set of step lengths; the chute's size changes year to year. Settling it needs an owner decision to state the chute as a seasonal range (e.g. the park's 'short pitch to 250 ft / short pitch to 300+ ft') in every field, rather than a single figure.

New sources give only whole-route figures: a guide service states ~10 miles Paradise to summit; a 2020 carry-over trip logged 18.5 miles total up the Kautz and down the DC. No source states the Paradise-to-Camp Hazard mileage, so neither 5 nor 7 can be confirmed. A GPS track of the Paradise-Camp Hazard leg from two parties would settle it.

The ice on this line is the Kautz chute, whose size varies by season: one 2024 conditions report describes a ~50 ft mandatory lower step, other parties two full 60 m pitches, the park brief a lower step to ~250 ft and upper step to 300+ ft. No two sources give a total matching 259 m, 90 m, 300 ft or 400-450 ft. Settling needs an owner decision to express length as a seasonal range consistently.

results.correct_value: dist_km ~8.05 (about 5 mi one way, Paradise to summit)
results.evidence: A trip report describes the route as gaining a bit over 9,000 ft in only about 5 miles. A guide service's itinerary gives 2-3 miles from Paradise to high camp and 4-5 miles round trip on summit day (about 2-2.5 mi each way), i.e. roughly 5 mi one way. The stored 24.94 km (15.5 mi) is not a one-way figure; the itinerary (5 mi day 1, 8 mi summit-and-descent day 2) is consistent with ~5 mi one way.

The itinerary gives 5 miles for day 1 (Paradise to a Wilson Glacier high camp), while a guide service lists 2-3 miles for the Paradise-to-high-camp day. Only one source states the leg; a second (GPS track or route page) would settle it.

results.correct_value: dist_km ~16.1 (about 10 mi one way, White River to the summit); Liberty Cap waypoint distance unknown
results.evidence: The park route brief gives about 8 mi trailhead to Thumb Rock plus about 2.5 mi to Columbia Crest (10.5 mi). A guide service states ~10 miles from White River to the summit. So the one-way approach is about 10 mi (16.1 km), not 6 mi; the itinerary's 18 mi includes the carry-over descent. The Liberty Cap pin at mile 15 is impossible against both, and its own distance is unsourced, so it is set to unknown.

The park brief gives ~11,500 ft (matches gain_ft); a guide service states 10,000 ft; trip reports sum day gains to ~10,000 ft (3,100 + 3,300 + 3,600). Sources disagree, and per-day itinerary figures cannot be changed without a source stating them. A second source stating 11,500 ft (or a GPS-derived cumulative gain) would settle it.

results.fact: Elevation where the approach drops onto the Carbon Glacier
results.evidence: Three independent trip reports put the drop from Curtis Ridge onto the Carbon at about 7,200 ft (a 2018 party dropped onto the Carbon 'at about 7200', a ski party found the drop-off 'spot on at 7200 feet', a 2009 party camped on Curtis Ridge around 7,200 ft at the access point), and a route page says the ramp reaches the Carbon around 7,300 ft. The park brief's 7,600 ft is where parties leave the ridge crest, not where they reach the glacier. The approach_variants figure (roughly 7,300 ft) already agrees; pitch_detail's 7,600 is the outlier.
